138	# Investigation: API p95 latency doubled on Tue 2026-07-07 — why?
139	
140	## Problem
141	
142	- Decision informed: roll back the Tuesday deploy, or leave it and fix elsewhere.
143	- Falsifiable question: what explains the p95 latency increase for /checkout between 2026-07-06 and 2026-07-08 (ms, per-request, US region)?
144	- Success criteria: answered means one or more explanations account for the observed increase and survive a discriminating test.
145	- Stop condition: conclude when no named unresolved alternative could reverse the rollback decision.
146	- Effort budget: 25 queries.
147	
148	## Hypotheses
149	
150	| id | claim | Candidate explanation | Prediction if true | Prediction if false | Necessary prediction (failure refutes) | Cheapest adequate test | Data needed |
151	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
152	| H1 | causal | Tuesday deploy regressed the cache layer, causing the observed p95 step | p95 step aligns with deploy timestamp; cache hit rate drops | p95 shift precedes deploy or hit rate flat | the p95 step must not precede the deploy — a deploy cannot cause a step that happened before it | T1 | deploy log, cache metrics |
153	| H2 | causal | Traffic mix shifted toward uncached endpoints | share of cache-miss routes rises independently of deploy | route mix stable across the step | the cache-miss route share must rise at the step | T2 | request logs by route |
154	| H3 | descriptive (estimand: cache-miss route share on the new client version minus cache-miss route share on the old, 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-08) | Cache-miss route traffic is concentrated on the new client version | cache-miss route traffic concentrates in one client version | cache-miss route traffic is spread evenly across versions | the cache-miss route share must be higher on the new client version than on the old | T3 | request logs by user agent |

156	| H5 | data-artifact | The 07-07 21:00–23:00 `/checkout` log shortfall is a logging-pipeline gap, not a traffic drop | an independent request counter shows normal traffic in that window | the independent counter also shows a dip | the load balancer's counter must not dip when the logs do | T6 | LB request counter |
157	
158	## Sources
159	
160	| id | Origin (file, query, system) | Acquired | Coverage notes |
161	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
162	| S1 | deploy log `deploys/2026-07-07.log` | 2026-07-08 09:00Z | full day |
163	| S2 | cache metrics dashboard export, 5-min grain | 2026-07-08 09:05Z | 10% request sample |
164	| S3 | raw request logs `logs/checkout-2026-07-0{6,7,8}.jsonl.gz` | 2026-07-08 09:10Z | all rows; user-agent field populated for only ~30% of rows |
165	| S4 | trace spans, Jaeger query `/checkout` 07-06..07-08 | 2026-07-08 10:40Z | 1% trace sampling |
166	| S5 | load balancer request counter, 1-hour grain | 2026-07-08 11:15Z | independent of the logging pipeline — used as the coverage baseline |
167

169	
170	- Collection method: dashboard aggregates from the metrics pipeline; raw request logs and traces available.
171	- Coverage matrix: the analysis compares hours × route, so request-log rows were counted at that grain across 07-06..07-08. 178	S5: UNKNOWN — same.
179	- Sensitivity checks performed: dashboard step cross-checked against raw logs (known positive: the step appears in both), so the dashboard is not blind to steps of this size.

182

188	| T3 | H3 | cache-miss route share higher on the new client version than on the old | group cache-miss route traffic by user agent | NON_DISCRIMINATING | user-agent populated for only ~30% of rows (Sources S3); cannot detect a shift smaller than ~25pp (S3 §5) |

192

194	
195	- 2026-07-08: added H4 (retrospective) after T2 evidence showed latency also rose on some cached routes. 196	- 2026-07-08: added H5 after the coverage matrix showed a `/checkout` log shortfall on 07-07 21:00–23:00. Not retrospective: it came from inspecting coverage, not a cause-outcome relationship.
197	
198	## Conclusion
199	
200	- Answer: the p95 increase is associated with a traffic-mix shift toward uncached routes starting 09:10 Tuesday; the deploy is not implicated, so do not roll back.
201	- Best supported: H2, via T2 and T5 (discriminating: the step co-occurs with the route-mix shift, precedes the deploy, and the mix shift reproduces most of the observed increase under reweighting).
202	- Per-hypothesis summary:
203	
204	  | id | claim | status | basis |
205	  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
206	  | H1 | causal | REFUTED | necessary timing prediction failed under an adequate test, T1. T1b also failed, but it tests a supporting prediction, not the necessary one, so it contributes nothing to the status either way |
207	  | H2 | causal | UNRESOLVED | best supported (T2, T5 CONSISTENT) |
208	  | H3 | descriptive | UNRESOLVED | T3 NON_DISCRIMINATING — user-agent coverage too sparse to detect a shift smaller than ~25pp, so nothing settled it. Registered descriptive with its estimand named, not causal: nothing assigned client version independently of traffic, so T3's contrast does not identify a causal effect and could not have refuted a causal version claim even at full coverage |
209	  | H4 (retrospective) | causal | REFUTED | its necessary majority-of-added-latency prediction failed under T4, on trace spans that had not informed it |
210	  | H5 | data-artifact | UNRESOLVED | best supported for the coverage gap (T6 CONSISTENT) |
211	- Limitations: what drove the traffic shift is unresolved (T3 NON_DISCRIMINATING — user-agent coverage too sparse); the 07-07 21:00–23:00 hours are excluded from rate denominators per H5/T6, which does not change the conclusion but narrows the window the step is measured over; the claim is associative — the route mix was not assigned by anything independent of latency, and no intervention was run, so "the mix shift is associated with the increase" is as far as this data reaches.
